==English==

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|hīr|hīʹər}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈhaɪ(.)ə/|a=RP}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-hire.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈhaɪɹ/|/ˈhɑɪ.əɹ/|a=GA}}
* {{hmp|en|higher|aa=most accents}}

===Etymology 1===
From {{inh|en|enm|hire}}, {{m|enm|hyre}}, {{m|enm|here}}, {{m|enm|hure}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hȳr|t=employment for wages; pay for service; interest on money lent}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hūʀiju|t=payment}}, from the verb {{m|gmw-pro|*hūʀijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hūzijaną}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kewHs-}} or {{m|ine-pro||*kweHs-}}. Compare {{cog|hit|𒆪𒊭𒀭|tr=kuššan-|t=fee, pay, wages, price}}.

Cognate with {{cog|fy|hier|t=hire}}, {{cog|nl|huur|t=lease, rental}}, {{cog|nds-de|Hüür|t=lease, rental}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|countable}} A [[person#Noun|person]] who has been [[hire#Verb|hired]], especially in a [[cohort]].
#: {{ux|en|We pair up each of our new '''hires''' with one of our original '''hires'''.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} The [[state#Noun|state]] of being hired, or having a [[job#Noun|job]]; [[employment]].
#: {{synonyms|en|employ}}
#: {{ux|en|When my grandfather retired, he had over twenty mechanics in his '''hire'''.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} [[payment|Payment]] for the [[temporary#Adjective|temporary]] [[use#Noun|use]] of something.
#: {{ux|en|The sign offered pedalos on '''hire'''.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable|obsolete}} [[reward#Noun|Reward]].
#* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=II|canto=VIII|passage=I vvill him reaue of armes, the victors '''hire''', / And of that ſhield, more vvorthy of good knight; / For vvhy ſhould a dead dog be deckt in armour bright?}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare As You Like It|act=II|scene=iii|lines=682–683|passage=I have five hundred crovvns, / The thrifty '''hire''' I ſav'd under your father {{...}}}}
#* {{RQ:King James Version|Luke|10|7|passage=The labourer is worthy of his '''hire'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|author=Samuell Hieron|chapter=The Worth of the Water of Life. [[w:David|Dauids]] Longing, and Dauids Loue. The Good Fight. [[[w:Second Epistle to Timothy|II. Tim[othy]]] 4. 7.]|title=The Sermons of Master Samuell Hieron,{{nb...|Formerly Collected together by Himselfe, and Published in One Volume in His Life-time. Hereunto are Annexed of the Same Authors, 1. The Preachers Plea. 2. An Answere to a Popish Rime. 3. Meditations Touching Death. 4. The Doctrine of the Beginning of Christ, in Forme of a Catechisme. 5. An Help vnto Deuotion. With Five Other of His Sermons hereunto Annexed.}}|location=London|publisher={{...|Printed by}} Iohn Beale [and [[w:John Legate|John Legatt]] printer to the [[w:University of Cambridge|Uniuersitie of Cambridge]] for Thomas Man, Ioyce Macham, Cantrell Legge, and Simon Waterson]|year=1619|year_published=1620|pages=222–223|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=RA00QAafAD8C&pg=PA223|oclc=1203219768|passage=I haue ſeene a pardon giuen to a man vpon the gallovves, but vvho ſo emboldeneth himſelfe thereuypon, perhaps the rope may be his '''hire''': it is not good to put it vpon the Pſalme of ''Miſerere'', and the neck-verſe, for ſometime he prooues no clarke.}}

===Etymology 2===
From {{inh|en|enm|hiren<id:to hire>}}, {{m|enm|hyren}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hȳrian|t=to hire}}, from the noun (see above). Compare {{cog|fy|hiere|t=to rent, lease}}, {{cog|nl|huren|t=to rent, lease}}, {{cog|nds|hüren|t=to rent}}, {{cog|da|hyre|t=to hire}}, {{cog|sv|hyra|t=to hire}}.

Eclipsed {{noncog|enm|souden|t=to hire, employ, enlist}}, borrowed from {{noncog|fro|souder}}, {{m|fro|soudre}}, {{m|fro|souldre|t=to take into employ, pay}}; see obsolete {{noncog|en|sold|t=salary, military pay}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive|chiefly|UK|and|Australia}} To [[obtain]] the [[service]]s of in return for [[fix]]ed [[payment]].
#: {{synonyms|en|rent}}
#: {{ux|en|We '''hired''' a car for two weeks because ours had broken down.}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=16|passage=“{{...}} She takes the whole thing with desperate seriousness. But the others are all easy and jovial—thinking about the good fare that is soon to be eaten, about the '''hired''' fly, about anything.”}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|chiefly|UK}} To [[occupy]] [[premise]]s in exchange for rent.
#: {{synonyms|en|rent}}
#* {{RQ:Thoreau Walden|chapter=Economy|passage=I do not mean to insist here on the disadvantage of '''hiring''' compared with owning, but it is evident that the savage owns his shelter because it costs so little, while the civilized man '''hires''' his commonly because he cannot afford to own it; nor can he, in the long run, any better afford to '''hire'''.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To employ; to obtain the services of (a person) in exchange for [[remuneration]]; to give someone a [[job]].
#: {{ux|en|The company had problems when it tried to '''hire''' more skilled workers.}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=10|passage=The skipper Mr. Cooke had '''hired''' at Far Harbor was a God-fearing man with a luke warm interest in his new billet and employer, and had only been prevailed upon to take charge of the yacht after the offer of an emolument equal to half a year's sea pay of an ensign in the navy.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To exchange the services of for remuneration.
#: {{ux|en|They '''hired''' themselves out as day laborers.  They '''hired''' out their basement for Inauguration week.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|chiefly|UK}} To accomplish by paying for services.
#: {{ux|en|After waiting two years for her husband to finish the tiling, she decided to '''hire''' it done.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To accept employment.
#: {{ux|en|They '''hired''' out as day laborers.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} {{lb|en|neologism}} (in the Jobs-to-be-Done Theory) To buy something in order for it to perform a function, to do a job
#: {{ux|en|They '''hired''' a milkshake.}}
